summary: Makanza (Mankanza) territory in Equateur lies along the main Congo River channel, far from the eastern conflict zones; no armed group is reported to hold any territory there. The territory seat Makanza town is administered by the state, with the Congolese National Police handling day-to-day order and FARDC/naval elements present on the river. Historical banditry and river piracy have been reported but there is no evidence of a non-state actor exercising control. Rural villages (Makanza and Mampoko health zones) are assessed as default state (PNC) presence with low-medium confidence given scarce reporting.

zones.description: Makanza (Mankanza) town, territory seat, all quarters
zones.evidence: Territory seat with state administration on the Congo River; no reports of armed-group presence in 2025-2026 searches. Policing assumed by PNC with FARDC/naval elements present; past banditry has not translated into non-state control.

zones.description: Rural villages of Makanza health zone along the Congo River and islands (Bonkoti/Lusengo, Ngomba/Mobeka, Konongo, Ebodjela/Paris, Lobengo, Bolombo, Malunza, etc.)
zones.evidence: No reports of armed-group activity in rural Makanza territory as of 2026; state presence through police posts and secteur administration, with customary chiefs handling local disputes. River banditry/piracy is occasional and not territorial.

zones.description: Southern villages in Mampoko health zone (Nganda Mpaka, Limbila)
zones.evidence: Remote riverine villages with no reported armed-group activity; assessed as default state presence.
